overview: Outer Caroline Island wayfinding communities sustain specialised canoe and navigation traditions. Satawal and Puluwat examples represent related local practices, not a single empire.

items.text: A Satawal teaching model arranges 32 horizon points associated with rising and setting stars or constellations, alongside swell directions.
In etak navigation, a reference island is imagined shifting against star bearings as the canoe travels. The method helps organise a journey mentally.
Traditional outrigger canoes can reverse sailing direction without turning the hull around. Sailing therefore combines vessel design with coordinated handling.
A master craftsperson guides canoe construction, shaping the hull with an adze. Coconut-fibre cord and pandanus sails form part of the vessel technology.
The Yap Traditional Navigation Society supports preservation and teaching. Navigation remains a living field of skill rather than a vanished technology.

sources.title: Ben Finney: Nautical Cartography and Traditional Navigation in Oceania
